name: One-Pan Sloppy Joe Casserole

ingredients.buy: 1/2 cup plus 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar
9 bell peppers, diced (about half red, half green)

prose.intro_html:
Sloppy joes are one of the great budget dinners of all time, but a pile of saucy meat on a squishy bun does not exactly hold up in a meal-prep container by Thursday. So we did the sensible thing and turned the whole idea into a casserole. Same seasoned tomato and beef flavor you grew up on, except the bun is baked right on top as a golden layer of biscuit, and the whole thing goes together in one oven-safe skillet.

Here is the part I like. It is honest food built from cheap, boring pantry stuff, tomato sauce, ketchup, a little brown sugar and vinegar, ground turkey, and a can or two of refrigerated biscuits. Nothing fancy, nothing you have to hunt for. It scales cleanly to 14 servings, it reheats like a champ, and it lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein per serving. That is a real dinner doing real work.
prose.shop_smart:
This one rewards you for buying the plain stuff. Here is how I fill the cart:

  • Ground turkey is the anchor. You need 4 2/3 pounds for the full batch, so grab the larger family packs rather than the little one-pound trays.
  • Biscuits come in cans, and you want 21 halved, which works out to about three 8-count cans. Buy three cans and you have a couple of biscuits left to spare, no partial-can math.
  • Tomato sauce, ketchup, and tomato paste are the backbone of the sauce. Store brands are fine here. Nobody at your table will ever know.
  • Bell peppers keep this from being one-note. The recipe wants 9, roughly half red and half green, so shop the loose bin and pick what looks good rather than the pricier pre-cut cups.
  • Onion powder, black pepper, salt, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, and Worcestershire are all shelf-stable seasonings you likely already own. If you are stocking from scratch, they carry over into a dozen other dinners.
  • Shredded cheddar, about 1 pound 2 ounces total. A block you shred yourself melts nicer, but bagged shredded is the faster move on a prep day.
prose.make_it:
One skillet, one oven, start to finish. Here is the run of it.

  1. Heat the oven to 375 degrees. In a bowl, whisk together the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, onion powder, black pepper, and salt. Set that sauce aside so the flavors get acquainted.
  2. Get your oven-safe skillet hot over medium-high. Add the minced garlic and stir about 1 minute until it smells good. Add the diced onion and the tomato paste and cook 1 to 2 minutes, letting the paste darken a shade. Add the diced bell peppers and cook everything 3 to 5 minutes to soften.
  3. Push the vegetables to the side and lay the ground turkey in the open space. Let it sear undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes, then break it into pieces and cook until browned and the internal temperature hits 165 degrees.
  4. Drop the heat to medium-low and pour in the sauce. Stir until the meat and vegetables are coated.
  5. Let it simmer 5 to 6 minutes so it thickens slightly. Scatter the shredded cheddar over the top. Peel each biscuit in half to make two thinner rounds and arrange them over the mixture so the top is covered.
  6. Slide the skillet into the oven and bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the biscuits are golden brown and cooked through in the middle. Let it settle a few minutes before you portion it out.
prose.portion_html:
This is a weigh-the-pot job, and it is the only way to keep 14 containers honest. Once the casserole comes out and rests, set your empty skillet weight aside in your head and weigh the full cooked skillet, or just weigh the finished food straight into a bowl on the scale. Take that total weight, divide by 14, and that number is your target per container.

Then portion by the scale, not by eye. Spoon meat and sauce into each of the 14 containers to that target weight, and make sure every container gets its fair share of biscuit topping and cheese, not just whoever you scoop first. Eyeballing is how the last three containers end up sad. The scale is how all 14 come out to {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein like the label says.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the math that matters. This casserole runs about ${{cost_ps}} per serving, and for that you get a hot, filling dinner with {{protein}} grams of protein, not a snack, not a side, a plate that actually holds you until morning.

Compare that to the drive-thru value meal or the sad gas-station sandwich and it is not close. Cook once, portion 14, and you have bought yourself two weeks of dinners for the price of one night out. That is the whole Thrifty Crew idea in one skillet.

Reduce the heat to medium-low, pour in the sauce, and stir to combine.
Simmer 5 to 6 minutes until slightly thickened. Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over top, peel each biscuit in half into two thinner rounds, and arrange them over the mixture.
